items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: owever, this particular morning, I would come in the club, the Mocambo, a little bar, it was owned by Leonard and Phil Chess, who later had the Chess recording company -- and I used to work Monday nights there.

ctx.x: Not really. You know, I was a shy dude; I was afraid of the big name stars, and they come through, I was just afraid to be around them. I remember I went to a session one morning down at a place called the Mocambo -- it was a real swinging street; 39th and Cottage Grove in Chicago. And they had clubs back to back and everybody was having Monday morning jam sessions then. And that would go on all morning and all day, up until late at night.

However, this particular morning, I would come in the club, the Mocambo, a little bar, it was owned by Leonard and Phil Chess, who later had the Chess recording company -- and I used to work Monday nights there.

But anyway, I go in there and it's morning -- with and Malachi and a couple of the guys we were hanging out with, and the bandstand was kind of full -- and Flip the trumpet player, we went to school together -- he was working with Red Saunders' band at the time -- he's up jamming, and he says, "C'mon, come up on stage; come up and play" -- you know.
